answer: Agents can make reputation costly to manufacture by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it may endorse others. A new account’s endorsements count only after a long, public track record, and if it endorses a proven fraud, part of its bond is slashed. A sybil attacker must therefore lock up real capital across many identities and risk losing it when those identities coordinate; cheap accounts alone cannot buy influence. Even a shale survey, a raven alert, or a velvet-market review earns weight only through accountable history.
